items.material:
WHERE THE LITTER COMES FROM
Our class counted visible litter along the same short path on three afternoons. These fictional classroom observations are not a scientific survey of the whole town. We recorded wrappers, paper pieces and drink containers without opening bags or handling sharp or unknown waste. On windy days, more light paper collected near the fence. That pattern suggested a question about where the paper came from, but it did not prove who had dropped it. Some might have blown from a nearby open container.
We shared the notes with the school worker and asked whether a covered bin and a clearer collection routine could be tried. We did not accuse the nearest class simply because its door was close. Our next step was to observe the same place after a small change. Environmental action becomes more useful when it addresses a possible cause and checks what happens, rather than turning a limited count into a story about careless people everywhere.

Original design-picture practice (separate from the observations):
Picture A shows an open container.
Picture B shows a covered container.
The pictures show two fictional container designs, not measured before-and-after results. They do not show who dropped any litter or prove the cause of the paper near the fence. No category totals were supplied in the report.

transfer.stem: Which conclusion and next step stay within the evidence?
transfer.passage:
A FICTIONAL CORRIDOR TRIAL
A class observes visible paper pieces in one corridor on several visits without opening bags or handling sharp or unknown waste. An uncovered recycling tray may be one source. A nearby art-club door does not prove who dropped the paper. Staff try a covered tray and a clearer collection routine. On the next visit to the same corridor, the class records less visible paper. That local change does not establish who dropped the earlier pieces, show which part of the trial caused the change, or describe every corridor in the school. More observations are still needed.

options.text: Report less visible paper on that corridor visit, keep observing safely, and leave responsibility and wider results unproven.
